Single sign-on is the organization's own company or university login.

git.forge_rate_limited: {{host}} is a product name such as GitHub or GitLab, or a server name such as gitlab.example.org.
git.forge_redirect_refused: {{host}} is a product name such as GitHub or GitLab, or a server name such as gitlab.example.org. {{target}} is a server name such as cdn.example.org.

git.import_cancelled: Shown when the person cancels cloning or importing a Git repository.
git.repository_not_found: {{host}} is a product name such as GitHub or GitLab, or a server name such as gitlab.example.org.
git.ssh_key_rejected: {{host}} is a product name such as GitHub or GitLab, or a server name such as gitlab.example.org.
git.tls_failed: {{host}} is a product name such as GitHub or GitLab, or a server name such as gitlab.example.org.
git.tracked_secret_files: Shown when Publish stops before uploading. {{files}} is up to five project file paths separated by commas, such as .env, deploy/server.pem, followed by (+N) when there are more. Keep the paths and the (+N) exactly as they are.

project.linked_in_app_data: Shown when a folder opened in place and Oleafly's own data folder end up one inside the other, usually after one of them was moved. {{folder}} is only the folder's name, never a full path. Either folder can be the one inside.
project.folder_read_only: Shown when Oleafly can't save, create, rename, move, copy, import or delete something in a folder opened in place because part of that folder is read-only. {{name}} is a path inside the project, such as figures/plot.png or project.json. It can be a file that doesn't exist yet (a new file, or where a move, copy or import was going), a read-only folder that was being moved, or, when a delete stops partway, the item Oleafly couldn't remove, such as figures/plot.png inside a read-only figures folder. "Its folder" is the folder that holds {{name}}. "The folder you opened" is the whole folder opened in place, not the subfolder. The second sentence points to Copy into library, which is on the read-only banner and in the folder's menu in the Library. The banner only shows when the whole folder is read-only, so don't mention it.

zotero.library_not_readable: Shown when a Zotero API key is valid but has no access to the user's personal library. "Allow library access" is the checkbox label on the key's page at zotero.org. Keep it in English, because zotero.org shows it in English.
zotero.user_mismatch: Shown when the Zotero user ID typed in Settings differs from the account the API key belongs to. {{keyUserId}} is the key's numeric user ID and {{userId}} is the number the user typed.
zotero.too_large: Shown when the Zotero library is bigger than one import allows. The RDF export is Zotero's File, Export Collection, Zotero RDF option.

collab.suggestion_role: Shown when someone whose role is reviewer or commenter tries to create, rename, move or delete a file in a shared project. Use the same words as the collaboration error with the same name.

notebook.code_needed: {{engine}} is Quarto or Calepin. Code is the per-project setting in the Compile menu that lets the R, Python or Julia code in the document run. Its Off choice is what "code is off" means.
notebook.quarto_missing: Settings > Engines > Quarto is the path to the Quarto tab. Use the same words as the Settings window title and the Engines section name, joined with >.
notebook.calepin_missing: Settings > Engines > Calepin is the path to the Calepin tab. Use the same words as the Settings window title and the Engines section name, joined with >.
notebook.install_unverified: {{tool}} is Quarto or Calepin. The downloaded archive did not match its checksum.
notebook.quarto_outdated: Settings > Engines > Quarto is the path to the Quarto tab. Use the same words as the Settings window title and the Engines section name, joined with >.
notebook.would_overwrite: {{file}} is a path inside the project. Quarto's working file is the intermediate .tex or .typ it writes next to the document.
notebook.missing_glyphs_cjk_one: CJKmainfont, pdf-engine: tectonic and {{font}} are literal YAML the person types. Keep them unchanged.
notebook.missing_glyphs_cjk_other: CJKmainfont, pdf-engine: tectonic and {{font}} are literal YAML the person types. Keep them unchanged.
notebook.not_project_input: project: render and _quarto.yml are literal Quarto YAML. Keep them unchanged.

provider_credit.failed: {{provider}} is an AI provider name such as OpenRouter or DeepSeek. Keep it unchanged.

mathpix.rejected: {{reason}} is Mathpix's own English error text
mathpix.http_error: {{status}} is a numeric HTTP status code such as 502
mathpix.pdf_too_large_ipc: Shown when the webview hands a PDF to Mathpix as a long list of numbers (a fallback on some Linux systems) and the file is over 16 MB; the usual limit is 256 MB

terminal.wsl_missing: WSL is Windows Subsystem for Linux. Keep the name WSL. Shown in the terminal when the person picked WSL as the shell.
terminal.wsl_no_distro: WSL is Windows Subsystem for Linux. Keep the name WSL. A Linux distribution is an installed Linux system such as Ubuntu.
terminal.git_bash_missing: Git Bash and Git for Windows are product names. Keep them verbatim.
terminal.pwsh_missing: PowerShell 7 is a product name. Keep it verbatim.
terminal.shell_path_missing: {{path}} is the file path of the shell program the person entered in Settings. Shown in the terminal.

shell_command.path_failed: Windows only. PATH is the environment variable name. Keep it verbatim. {{directory}} is a folder path.
shell_command.in_use: Windows only. {{path}} is the oleafly.exe file. oleafly is the command name.

explain.missing_dollar: _, ^ and $...$ are LaTeX syntax the writer types. Keep them exactly as written.
explain.unbalanced_braces: { and } are LaTeX syntax the writer types. Keep them exactly as written.
explain.runaway_argument: } and \end{...} are LaTeX syntax the writer types. Keep them exactly as written.
explain.double_superscript: ^ and the examples x^{a}^{b} and x^{ab} are LaTeX syntax. Keep them exactly as written.
explain.double_subscript: _ and the examples x_{a}_{b} and x_{ab} are LaTeX syntax. Keep them exactly as written.
explain.extra_alignment_tab: & is the LaTeX character that separates table columns. Keep it exactly as written.
explain.misplaced_alignment_tab: & and \& are LaTeX syntax the writer types. Keep them exactly as written.
explain.no_line_to_end: The \\ at the start is the LaTeX line break command. Keep it exactly as written.
explain.too_many_floats: A float is a figure or table LaTeX can move to fit the page. \clearpage and [htbp] are LaTeX syntax. Keep them exactly as written.
explain.file_not_found_tectonic: Tectonic and latexmk are compiler names. Keep them exactly as written.
explain.environment_mismatch: \begin{...}, \end{...}, \begin and \end are LaTeX syntax. Keep them exactly as written.
explain.missing_item: itemize, enumerate, description and \item are LaTeX names. Keep them exactly as written.
explain.float_moved: A float is a figure or table LaTeX can move to fit the page. [htbp] is LaTeX syntax. Keep it exactly as written.
explain.float_too_large: A float is a figure or table LaTeX can move to fit the page. width=\linewidth is LaTeX syntax. Keep it exactly as written.
explain.pythontex_failed: PythonTeX and latexmk are program names. Keep them exactly as written. Allow external commands is the button in the banner above the editor, so use the same words as that button.
explain.biber_no_entry: {{entry}} is a citation key from the document's bibliography. Biber is a program name.
explain.biber_file_missing: {{file}} is a file name. Biber is a program name, and \addbibresource is a LaTeX command. Keep them exactly as written.
explain.biber_version_mismatch: {{found}} and {{expected}} are version numbers. Biber and biblatex are program names.
explain.biber_needs_run: Biber and biblatex are program names. Keep them exactly as written.
explain.citation_missing: {{name}} is a citation key from the document. Keep the backticks around it.
explain.reference_missing: {{name}} is a label from the document. Keep the backticks around it.
